datasets.name: Globally averaged marine surface CO₂ (annual mean and growth rate)
datasets.provider: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory, Carbon Cycle Greenhouse Gases group
datasets.license: Public domain (US Government work). NOAA GML asks that the data providers be contacted and credited.
datasets.citation: Lan, X., Tans, P. and K.W. Thoning: Trends in globally-averaged CO2 determined from NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory measurements.
datasets.description: Dry-air mole fraction of carbon dioxide averaged over a network of marine boundary-layer sampling sites, reported as an annual mean with a published uncertainty, and as an annual growth rate computed by the provider from December-to-December differences.
datasets.geographicCoverage: Global — marine boundary layer reference network
datasets.updateFrequency: Annual, with monthly means published through the year; the most recent year is preliminary pending recalibration of standard gases.
datasets.notes: The marine boundary layer reference network deliberately excludes sites close to strong local sources, so this is not the mole fraction over any particular city or forest. It is the well-mixed background.

datasets.name: Globally averaged marine surface CH₄ (annual mean)
datasets.provider: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory, Carbon Cycle Greenhouse Gases group
datasets.license: Public domain (US Government work). NOAA GML asks that the data providers be contacted and credited.
datasets.citation: Lan, X., Thoning, K.W. and Dlugokencky, E.J.: Trends in globally-averaged CH4 determined from NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory measurements.
datasets.description: Dry-air mole fraction of methane averaged over the marine boundary-layer network, reported as an annual mean with a published uncertainty.
datasets.geographicCoverage: Global — marine boundary layer reference network
datasets.updateFrequency: Annual, with monthly means published through the year; the most recent year is preliminary.

datasets.name: Globally averaged marine surface N₂O (annual mean)
datasets.provider: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory, Carbon Cycle Greenhouse Gases group
datasets.license: Public domain (US Government work). NOAA GML asks that the data providers be contacted and credited.
datasets.citation: Lan, X., Thoning, K.W. and Dlugokencky, E.J.: Trends in globally-averaged N2O determined from NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory measurements.
datasets.description: Dry-air mole fraction of nitrous oxide averaged over the marine boundary-layer network, reported as an annual mean with a published uncertainty.
datasets.geographicCoverage: Global — marine boundary layer reference network
datasets.updateFrequency: Annual; the most recent year is preliminary.
datasets.notes: The global N₂O record starts much later than the CO₂ and CH₄ records because the global marine-boundary-layer product for N₂O begins in 2001, not because nitrous oxide was unmeasured before then.

datasets.name: NOAA Annual Greenhouse Gas Index (AGGI)
datasets.citation: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory, The NOAA Annual Greenhouse Gas Index (AGGI).
datasets.description: Direct radiative forcing from the long-lived greenhouse gases — CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, CFCs, HCFCs and HFCs — computed from measured global mole fractions, expressed both in W m⁻² and as an index normalised to 1990.
datasets.notes: The AGGI is a derived index, not a measurement. Its inputs are measured mole fractions; the step from mole fraction to forcing uses published radiative-transfer expressions, and the index is that forcing divided by its 1990 value.

datasets.name: GISTEMP v4 — GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (global land–ocean means)
datasets.provider: NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies
datasets.citation: GISTEMP Team, GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP), version 4. NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies.
datasets.description: Global surface temperature anomaly combining land station air temperature with sea surface temperature, expressed against the 1951–1980 base period.
datasets.updateFrequency: Monthly, around the middle of the following month
datasets.notes: GISTEMP is one of several independent global temperature analyses. They differ in how they treat sparsely sampled regions, particularly the Arctic, which is why their annual values are close but not identical.

datasets.name: Global Ocean Heat Content, 0–2000 m
datasets.provider: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
datasets.citation: Levitus, S. et al., NCEI Global Ocean Heat and Salt Content, NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information.
datasets.description: Yearly ocean heat content anomaly for the 0–2000 m layer of the world ocean and each hemisphere, with the provider's standard error, in units of 10²² joules.
datasets.geographicCoverage: World ocean, and northern and southern hemispheres separately
datasets.notes: The yearly 0–2000 m series begins in 2005 because that is when Argo float coverage became dense enough to support it. NCEI's column documentation states the units as 10²² joules; it does not state the reference climatology on that page, so this repository does not assert one.

datasets.name: Sea Ice Index, version 4 — Northern Hemisphere monthly extent
datasets.provider: National Snow and Ice Data Center
datasets.license: Freely available for research and education; NSIDC asks that the data set be cited.
datasets.citation: Fetterer, F., Knowles, K., Meier, W. N., Savoie, M. and Windnagel, A. K.: Sea Ice Index, Version 4. NSIDC, Boulder, Colorado USA.
datasets.description: Monthly mean sea ice extent and area for the Northern Hemisphere, derived from passive-microwave satellite brightness temperatures. Extent counts every grid cell with at least 15 per cent ice concentration.
datasets.notes: Extent and area are different quantities and the file publishes both. Extent counts a partly covered cell in full; area does not. The two diverge most in summer, when melt ponds on the ice surface are read as open water.

datasets.name: Global mean sea level anomaly from satellite altimetry
datasets.license: Public domain (US Government work). NOAA asks for the acknowledgement 'Altimetry data are provided by NOAA Laboratory for Satellite Altimetry.'
datasets.citation: NOAA Laboratory for Satellite Altimetry, Global mean sea level anomaly, Radar Altimeter Database System (RADS).
datasets.description: Global mean sea level anomaly measured by the TOPEX/Poseidon, Jason-1, Jason-2, Jason-3 and Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich radar altimeters, with the seasonal signal retained and no glacial isostatic adjustment applied.
datasets.geographicCoverage: Global ocean between roughly 66°S and 66°N, the altimeter footprint
datasets.updateFrequency: Roughly every 10 days, one value per altimeter cycle
datasets.notes: This is the series without the glacial isostatic adjustment correction, which is why its published trend differs from GIA-corrected series by roughly 0.3 mm per year. The altimeter does not cover the polar oceans, and the record is a splice across five missions.

datasets.name: CODATA Internationally Recommended Values of the Fundamental Physical Constants (2022 adjustment)
datasets.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology
datasets.citation: Mohr, P. J., Newell, D. B., Taylor, B. N. and Tiesinga, E., CODATA Recommended Values of the Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022. NIST.
datasets.description: The internationally recommended values of the fundamental physical constants, with standard uncertainties, from the 2022 CODATA adjustment. Constants that define an SI unit are marked exact.
datasets.notes: Seven constants are exact by definition of the SI and carry no uncertainty. The rest are measured, and their uncertainties are the reason the adjustment is repeated.
